name: Living Widgets
summary: Dashboard widgets become googly-eyed characters that doze until Pulse makes them look — the checkout card literally slumps.
look: Real light-mode UI cards on warm paper, each with a pair of googly eyes. Pupil direction is the storytelling device; emotion comes from tilt, squash and brows, never mouths.

components.name: Eyed widget
components.role: any chart card + two googly eyes; pupil direction = attention

components.name: Sleep eyes
components.role: closed arcs = an unwatched dashboard (the pain)

components.name: Hero card
components.role: the one anomalous metric, scaled up, with brows and a sweat drop

components.name: Anomaly readout
components.role: −18% in coral + mono meta line (since 09:42 · deploy #2231)

components.name: Decision pill
components.role: coral Roll back + ghost Acknowledge, pressed by a real cursor

components.name: Happy row
components.role: the widget cast lined up with smiling eyes under the CTA

motion.name: Pupil snap
motion.how: pupils tween to a look-at target in 0.12 s power4.out, 20 ms stagger; always on a downbeat (every 0.5 s at 120 BPM)

motion.name: Slump & squash
motion.how: hero card rotates to −3° with a 6 % vertical squash, 0.4 s back.out(2); the break in the line is drawn over one beat

motion.name: Idle blink
motion.how: each widget blinks (scaleY 1→0.1→1, 0.14 s) at random 2–4 bar intervals; blinks are quantised to 8ths so the wall pulses with the hi-hat

story: Hook: a wall of 38 widgets staring everywhere or asleep. Reveal: all pupils snap to the Acme mark on the drop. Proof: the checkout card slumps with wide eyes at its −18% break after deploy #2231 while you press Roll back. CTA: the cast lines up smiling under 'You ship. Pulse watches.'
adapt: Use your own dashboard cards, charts or table rows as the cast; keep the eyes the only addition. Your key metric becomes the hero card and your primary action becomes the button it looks at.

references.note: objects carry emotion through posture and timing
SaaS brand character used with restraint (Freddie's wink)

fit.risk: Cute can read as childish for enterprise buyers — keep the UI itself real and restrained, put personality only in eyes and posture, and never give the widgets mouths or voices.
